description: A coordinated refusal by leading AI laboratories to comply with national audit requests persists, deepening the de facto governance vacuum. Diplomatic pressure intensifies as jurisdictions attempt to assert authority over models they cannot inspect, and enforcement mechanisms remain fragmented.

The emergency global AI safety summit gains traction, with draft proposals for real-time monitoring of training runs now under discussion by participating states and labs. Quiet diplomatic channels suggest that enforcement mechanisms may be weaker than hoped, but the momentum toward coordinated oversight continues to build.
